title: Board action
description: The record of one agenda item taken up by a board, council, commission or committee: the body and meeting, who attended, the motions made, who moved and seconded them, each member's vote, recusals, public comment and the outcome. Motions, thresholds and voting follow the concepts of parliamentary procedure as described in Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised (RONR); the format records what happened and doesn't require any body to follow RONR, since bylaws, statutes and local rules take precedence. Works for corporate and nonprofit boards and for public bodies.

$schema.title: Schema
$schema.description: The `$id` of the schema the record follows, so a reader can tell what the record is without guessing. Optional; recordType and schemaVersion say the same thing.

recordType.title: Record type
recordType.description: Always board-action. Lets a reader (or validate()) tell the format apart from the others in this repository.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: The version of this format the record follows. Each version of the schema accepts only its own version string, so a record never silently passes against a schema it wasn't written for.

id.description: This record's identifier, unique within the system that created it. One record covers one agenda item, so a meeting with ten items has ten records sharing meeting.id.

externalIds.title: External identifiers
externalIds.description: Ids for this item in other systems, for example a legislative management system's file number or a board portal's item id.

updatedAt.description: When the record was last changed.

body.title: Body
body.description: The board, council, commission or committee that acted.

id.description: Identifier for the body, so records from many meetings can be grouped.

type.title: Body type
type.description: board-of-directors (a corporate or credit union board); board-committee (a committee of a board, such as audit or risk); board-of-trustees (nonprofit, pension or university trustees); city-council; county-board (board of supervisors or commissioners); school-board; planning-commission; authority-board (a public authority, district or agency board); advisory-committee; or other.

organization.description: The organization the body governs, for corporate and nonprofit boards.

jurisdiction.description: The public body's jurisdiction, if it is one.

publicBody.title: Public body
publicBody.description: Whether open-meetings (sunshine) law applies to the body. Public bodies have notice, public access and minutes obligations that private boards don't.

meeting.title: Meeting
meeting.description: The meeting at which the item was taken up.

id.description: Identifier for the meeting, shared by every item's record from the same meeting.

type.title: Meeting type
type.description: regular; special (called for specific business); emergency; annual; closed-session (a meeting or portion closed to the public under a stated legal basis; executive session); or workshop (study session, usually without final action).

scheduledStart.description: When the meeting was scheduled to start, as noticed.

calledToOrderAt.description: When the presiding officer called the meeting to order.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where the meeting was held, including any remote access details that were made public.
examples: Council Chambers, 100 Main St, and by video

remoteParticipation.title: Remote participation
remoteParticipation.description: Whether members could take part remotely. Whether remote members count toward quorum and may vote depends on the body's rules and, for public bodies, on law.

noticePostedAt.description: When public notice of the meeting was posted. Open-meetings laws set minimum notice periods, so this is what shows the notice was timely.

openToPublic.title: Open to the public
openToPublic.description: Whether the public could attend the part of the meeting where the item was taken up.

closedSessionBasis.title: Closed session basis
closedSessionBasis.description: The legal basis for closing the meeting to the public, cited as the body cites it, when the item was taken up in closed session.

presidingOfficerId.description: The member id of the presiding officer (chair, mayor, president) for this item.

quorum.title: Quorum
quorum.description: Whether enough voting members were present to act. Under RONR and most bylaws and statutes, a body without a quorum can't transact business; the validator flags motions recorded as adopted when present is below required.

required.title: Required
required.description: Voting members needed for a quorum, as set by bylaws, charter or statute (RONR's default for an organization with a defined membership is a majority of the members).

present.title: Present
present.description: Voting members present when the item was taken up. Can't exceed the voting members listed in members.

members.title: Members
members.description: Every member of the body for this meeting, voting and non-voting, with their attendance. Motions, votes and recusals refer to members by id so the validator can check them. Leave vacant seats out: votes based on the entire membership count the members listed here.

id.description: Identifier for the member, used by motions, votes and recusals.

name.title: Name
name.description: The member's name, as it appears in the minutes.

voting.title: Voting member
voting.description: Whether the member has a vote (false for ex officio non-voting members, such as a chief executive on a board or a student member on some school boards).

attendance.title: Attendance
attendance.description: present; remote (attended by phone or video); absent; excused (absent with the body's leave, which some bodies record differently); or arrived-late (present for this item but not for the whole meeting).

agendaItem.title: Agenda item
agendaItem.description: The item the body took up, as published on the agenda.

number.title: Number
number.description: The item's number on the agenda.

title.title: Title
examples: Award of contract for Alder Street water main replacement

section.title: Section
section.description: Where the item was on the agenda: consent (routine items adopted together by one motion without debate; any member may ask to remove an item); action; public-hearing; discussion; report (received for information); or closed-session.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The staff or sponsor summary of the item.

sponsor.description: Who brought the item (a member, a department head, a committee).

attachmentIds.description: Ids of the item's files in attachments (staff report, draft resolution, presentation).

publicComments.title: Public comments
publicComments.description: Comments from the public on the item, summarized as the minutes would.

speaker.title: Speaker
speaker.description: The speaker's name as they gave it; leave out when they didn't give one. Public comment is often a public record, but publish names only as your body's practice and law allow.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: What the speaker said, in brief.

motions.title: Motions
motions.description: Motions made on the item, in the order they were made: the main motion and any secondary motions (amendments, referral, postponement) that applied to it.

recusals.title: Recusals
recusals.description: Members who stepped aside from the item because of a conflict of interest, and why. A recusal is required or expected by conflict-of-interest law or policy and means the member takes no part. It differs from an abstention, where a member takes part but declines to vote: RONR (45:4) says a member with a direct personal or pecuniary interest not common to other members should not vote, but can't be compelled to abstain.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: financial-interest; family-relationship; employment (the member or a relative works for a party); prior-involvement (for example having acted as an advocate on the matter); appearance-of-conflict; or other.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: The disclosure, as stated on the record.

leftRoom.title: Left the room
leftRoom.description: Whether the member left the room during discussion and vote, as some laws and policies require.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: What the body decided on the item, as the minutes and any public summary will state it. The validator checks an approval is backed by an adopted motion.

result.title: Result
result.description: approved; approved-as-amended; denied; continued (to a later meeting, see continuedTo); referred (to a committee or staff); tabled (laid aside); received-and-filed (accepted for information, no action); or no-action.

actionNumber.title: Action number
actionNumber.description: The resolution, ordinance or minute order number assigned to the action.

continuedTo.description: The date the item was continued to, if continued.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: The decision in plain words, as it will appear in the minutes.

minutes.title: Minutes
minutes.description: The state of the minutes that record this action. Minutes are the official record once the body approves them.

status.title: Status
status.description: draft; approved (by the body, usually at its next meeting); or published.

approvedAt.description: When the body approved the minutes.

uri.title: Location
uri.description: Where the published minutes can be read.

status.description: Where the item is: scheduled (on an agenda); in-progress (taken up, not concluded); decided; minutes-approved (the minutes recording the decision are approved); or withdrawn (removed from the agenda). decided and minutes-approved need an outcome.

statusHistory.title: Status history
statusHistory.description: Every status the item has had, oldest first, ending at the current status (the validator checks both).

status.description: The status the record moved to, one of this format's status values.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Files that belong to the item: staff reports, draft resolutions, bid tabulations, presentations.

auditTrail.title: Audit trail
auditTrail.description: Recorded actions on the record, oldest first.

extensions.description: Local fields this format doesn't define, namespaced as <namespace>:<field>, for example examplecity:councilDistrict.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status values of this format, defined once so status and statusHistory use the same list. Where the item is: scheduled (on an agenda); in-progress (taken up, not concluded); decided; minutes-approved (the minutes recording the decision are approved); or withdrawn (removed from the agenda). decided and minutes-approved need an outcome.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: A motion: who made and seconded it, how it was voted on, the threshold it needed and the result.

id.description: Identifier for the motion, unique within the record, so secondary motions can point at it.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: main (brings business before the body); amend; substitute (an amendment that replaces the whole text); refer (to a committee); postpone (to a set time; postpone indefinitely is other); table (lay on the table); take-from-table; reconsider; rescind (or amend something previously adopted); or other.

text.title: Text
text.description: The motion as stated by the mover or as the chair put the question.

appliesToMotionId.description: The motion this one applies to, for amendments, referrals and other secondary motions. Must name another motion in this record.

movedBy.description: The member id of the mover.

secondedBy.description: The member id of the seconder. Leave out when there was no second or none was needed (RONR's rules for small boards and committees don't require seconds). A member can't second their own motion.

voteMethod.title: Vote method
voteMethod.description: voice; roll-call (each member's vote called and recorded by name); show-of-hands; ballot; electronic; or unanimous-consent (the chair asks if there is any objection and, hearing none, declares the motion adopted; RONR calls this general consent).

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: The vote needed to adopt, as set by RONR, bylaws or law. majority-of-votes-cast: more yes than no votes (RONR's default majority vote; abstentions don't count). two-thirds-of-votes-cast: yes at least twice no (RONR's two-thirds vote). majority-of-members-present and two-thirds-of-members-present: of the members present, so an abstention has the same effect as a no. majority-of-entire-membership and two-thirds-of-entire-membership: of all members in office, present or not. unanimous: no votes against. other: anything else (describe it in extensions).

votes.title: Votes
votes.description: Each member's vote. For a roll call, list every voting member, using absent or recused for those who didn't vote, so the record is complete (the validator checks this).

vote.title: Vote
vote.description: yes; no; abstain (present but declined to vote; RONR doesn't count it as a vote cast); absent (not present for this vote); or recused (stepped aside for a conflict; needs a matching entry in recusals).

tally.title: Tally
tally.description: The counted result, as announced. Must match the individual votes when both are given.

abstain.title: Abstain
abstain.description: Members who abstained. Counted 0 when left out.

absent.title: Absent
absent.description: Members absent for the vote. Counted 0 when left out.

recused.title: Recused
recused.description: Members recused from the vote. Counted 0 when left out.

result.title: Result
result.description: adopted; failed (RONR: the motion is lost); withdrawn (by the mover); ruled-out-of-order (by the chair); died-for-lack-of-second; tabled; postponed; or referred. The last three are for a motion disposed of by a secondary motion. The validator checks adopted and failed against the threshold.

decidedAt.description: When the chair announced the result.
